I am afraid I do not understand your question very well. If you have discrete locations you can still user a continuous model. If you are thinking of observing small areas, this can also be done.

Regards,
Haakon

Dear all,

I want to incorporate the spatial autocorrelation into my model. I used to use SPDE to get a continuous random field. Is there any model to obtain a discrete random field? i.e. I only want to focus on discrete survey locations.Will matern2d work? 

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Discrete random spatial effect f(s)
parts:
Yes, that is what we usually do to simulate data!

On the different streams: This is an altogether different problem! Not sure if there are any good solutions to this yet. 

What kind of data do you have? Space-time? Are the streams thick or thin (relative to their lengths)?

The big problem here is that streams are usually very very thin, so spatial modeling does not make much sense, as it is a 1-dimensional problem with multiple 1-dimensional streams intersecting. Or a fractal (fractional dimension)....

Haakon

These locations are in different streams, so I think the spatial effect should not be isotropic, but I don’t know how to deal with this kind of problem.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Discrete random spatial effect f(s)
parts:
Hi,

for river network data, one might consider 1D GRMFs linked at the
points where streams join. But there might be effects that are linked
to more general spatial features, and for those a regular 2D Matern
model can be suitable. A completem model might therefore be a
combination of both types of models. How to do this in general is an
open research problem, but I think there have been some recent papers
dealing with this (but not necessarily in an INLA context). I don't
have the references handy, but I believe people in Switzerland were
involved, either from EPFL (possibly Anthony Davison) or ETH (or
both!). I think Marian Scott (and/or others from Glasgow) has been
doing some work in this direction as well. I'm also working on this
problem with others, but nothing available yet.

Finn
